summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow for phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) end-to-end, then execute all resulting plans via wave-based execution, while also spinning up a parallel worktree for phase 69 planning.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed fully (research, Nyquist VALIDATION.md, D-07 scope decision, pattern mapping, 12 plans across 7 waves, plan-checker PASSED, all coverage gates green) and committed; execution proceeded through Wave 5 (9/12 plans done, plan 10 in flight) with all spot-checks and independent test re-runs passing; a separate git worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main.

repo: gsd-tools query commit sometimes reports commit_failed even though the commit landed cleanly — documented false negative, always verify via git log.

GSD plan:pre hooks include a UI capability gate that only activates if the phase's registry `when` condition classifies it as a net-new UI surface; the lower-level ui-plan-gate check can report block:true without ever being invoked.
worktree.baseRef config (head vs fresh/origin) determines whether executor worktrees see just-created PLAN.md files — must verify before dispatching any worktree executor.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree executors each need their own pnpm install (expensive); for phases with mostly single-plan waves, sequential execution on the main tree is more robust and just as correct when the planner made same-wave plans file-disjoint.
gap-analysis.plan-post check output can contain control chars that break the standard parser — run the check directly instead.

REQUIREMENTS.md checkbox tracking is fragile: individual plan executors can prematurely mark requirement IDs [x] complete before the acceptance criteria (e.g. service deletion in a later wave) are actually met — needs manual correction/spot-checking after each plan.

Plan 11's deletion of ipns.service.ts/file-metadata.service.ts/kind-cache.ts/useFileSize.ts has a much wider importer surface (~15+ files) than the planner scoped; several files (utils/fileTypes.ts, lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts, vault-settings.store.ts, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts) are unowned by any plan and must be migrated before deletion.

code.finding: resolveChildren's per-child skip-on-failure is security-sound: the target folder is gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is merely omitted from listing (availability tradeoff), never rendered with stale/attacker content; navigating into any child re-triggers the gate.
ROT-07 enforceResolved gate wired into resolvePublishedNode (root resolve) in plan 68.2-01.
ROT-07 enforceResolved gate wired into dfsFindFolder child loop in plan 68.2-01.
Pre-existing write-path enforceResolved gate, now joined by two new read-path gate sites from plan 68.2-01.

workflow: ScheduleWakeup delaySeconds must be computed from a freshly-fetched current time immediately before the call, not from an earlier timestamp in context — a stale-timestamp computation caused a wake to be scheduled 25 minutes late.

For security-critical or deviation-flagged plan output, independently re-run the acceptance tests rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported PASS — caught nothing wrong here but is the correct discipline.

When an executor reports a 'notable deviation' on security-adjacent code, read the actual implementation (not just the summary) to confirm invariants (e.g. that a gate error still propagates) before advancing to the next wave.
A stray/duplicate ScheduleWakeup that can't be retracted is safe to leave in place if the agent will recognize on wake that the work is already done and treat it as a no-op.
